To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maduramicin improved feed efficiency and increased water consumption, whereas salinomycin improved feed efficiency and decreased water consumption.
feeding maduramicin and salinomycin for 49 days, followed by a 2-day withdrawal ration, had no effect on broiler body weight, but did improve feed conversion.
maduramicin increased water consumption in broilers, and maduramicn or salinomycin improved the feed conversion ratio of broilers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of feeding ionophores in broilers.
the effects of feeding ionophores in the presence of a withdrawal ration on broiler chickens.
the effect of ionophores in a coccidiosis-free environment and not in the presence of a challenge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maduramicin and salinomycin are effective in controlling coccidiosis in broiler chickens.
maduramicin and salinomycin were equally effective in improving performance and reducing water consumption of broiler chickens.
maduramicin was more effective at increasing feed intake and improving feed efficiency than was salinomycin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of either maduramicin or salinomycin to the ration for the entire 49 days improved feed efficiency.
maduramicin is more efficacious than salinomycin, and that the withdrawal ration should be fed for 3 days.
the inclusion of maduramicin or salinomycin into the feed of male and female coccidia-free broilers improved feed efficiency and had no effect on body weight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maduramicin and salinomycin have similar effects in the absence of coccidia.
the use of either salinomycin or maduramicn for the duration of the experiment did not affect final body weight, feed intake, feed efficiency, or mortality.
the use of either ionophores for coccidia control in broilers is not necessary if a withdrawal ration is used.
